I read pp. 85-86 and the Lean. cylindricalCurl matches (7.37), frame term included. vectorPotential is C_m e^{ikmΦ}, and curlRemainder is curl_*(C_m), exactly as (7.38) defines r_m. longitudinal_identity, with phaseFactor = Ki, is (7.39). The class, divergence, support and weight clauses are all stated: CurlClassBounds, UniformPrimaryWeights, potential_class, CopyAngularInvariance, commonGraph_physical_curl and pressure_amplitude_eq_source. Hypotheses can be met (ScaledGraph.geometry, PrimaryPulseBounds). I added the skeptics' θ-invariance declarations. For clause (v) I used pressure_amplitude_eq_source in place of pressure_scaling, which only relates two chart weights. longitudinal_class is never used downstream, but it still states the clause. The verdict and relation stand.

findings.summary: No single declaration bundles Lemma 7.7. Its clauses are separate theorems over an abstract StripData/CylindricalGeometry, and the paper's inputs ((6.32), Lemma 7.1, 1/(km) ≲ ε^{1/2}) become explicit hypotheses.

WaveClass is only the weighted-bound part of Def. 6.5 (no ∂_θ = 0, no support). The core is true, but the claim that θ-independence of r_m is not stated is wrong: CopyAngularInvariance states it for C_m, r_m and a_m, and the tsupport lemmas cover supports.

The auditor flagged that Lean's r_m is the full curl_*(C_m), θ-derivatives included, while the paper displays a θ-free formula. This is no difference: the paper defines r_m by (7.38) itself, and the display is derived from that using θ-independence.
The docstrings cite candidate-manuscript numbering ('Formula (30)', 'Lemma 9.2's curl remainder', 'Lemma 8.8'), not (7.38) and Lemma 7.7. This affects traceability only.
WaveClass also omits Def. 6.5's lift-compatibility (6.20) across overlapping chart representations and bounds only on s.domain. Lemma 7.7 inherits this from the Def. 6.5 encoding.
